criteria.text: `src/types.ts`'s `Person` type gains four optional string fields: `party`, `office`, `uf`, `wikidata`. `pnpm typecheck` passes with `seed.json` carrying all four on at least one entry.

All 27 entries in `seed.json` gain a `wikidata` QID. `party`, `office` and `uf` are filled by hand where they apply (a person with no current office may omit `office`; a national office may omit `uf`). No test asserts the specific values chosen for any real person — only that the mechanism echoing them works (AC4/AC5).

`src/server.ts` exports a pure `withSeedFields(row, seedMap?)`, defaulting to a `Map` built once at module load from the real `seed.json`; `GET /api/people`'s handler maps every DB row through it before responding.

A unit test on `withSeedFields`, called with a synthetic `seedMap` the test constructs (not real `seed.json`), proves: a field present on the seed entry is echoed; a field absent from the seed entry is omitted from the result, never present as `null`; `wikidata` is never echoed even when the synthetic entry carries one; a row whose `id` has no entry in the map is returned unchanged.

An integration test on `GET /api/people` (existing `app`, fixture-seeded DB) proves every row's keys are a subset of `['aliases', 'id', 'name', 'office', 'party', 'uf']` and never include `wikidata` — a structural check that holds regardless of which fields the real `seed.json` currently fills for `lula`/`tarcisio`/`bolsonaro`.
`docs/sources.md`'s "Tracked people" section states the `party`, `office`, `uf` and `wikidata` fields, and that the first three are echoed by `/api/people` while `wikidata` is not.
`docs/api.md`'s `/api/people` row or its surrounding prose names `party`/`office`/`uf` as optional, additive fields, consistent with the existing "the contract is stable" sentence.

`test/docs-drift.test.ts` needs no new criterion: it already asserts the tracked-seed-field list (`camaraId`, `senadoId`, `exclude`) is documented, and none of `party`/`office`/`uf`/`wikidata` are fields a collector reads, so that specific test is unaffected. AC6/AC7 above are the new, issue-specific documentation criteria.
